name: Crisp
tagline: A self-funded, all-in-one shared inbox that bundles live chat, WhatsApp, and an AI chatbot into one workspace price.
tldr: Crisp is an omnichannel customer messaging platform combining a website chat widget, shared team inbox, email, and social/WhatsApp channels with an AI chatbot layer (credit-metered) on top.

Pricing is per-workspace rather than strictly per-seat, running Free ($0, 2 seats) through Mini ($45/mo), Essentials ($95/mo), and Plus ($295/mo, marked 'Best Value'), each bundling a set number of seats plus a pool of AI credits for automated conversations.
Self-funded and profitable since founding — Crisp has taken no venture capital, founded in Nantes/Paris, France by Baptiste Jamin and Valerian Saliou, and runs lean at roughly 20 employees.

Independent review scores vary sharply by platform: strong on G2 and Capterra for ease of use and support responsiveness, but a notably rougher 1.9/5 on Trustpilot driven by billing and cancellation complaints.
Positioned as a budget-friendly alternative to Intercom/Zendesk for small-to-mid businesses that want live chat, shared inbox, and basic AI automation without enterprise-tier pricing.
keyFeatures: Shared team inbox unifying website chat, email, and connected social/messaging channels in one thread view
AI chatbot with a credit-based automation budget scaling by plan (from ~90 automated conversations on Mini to ~1,350 on Plus)
Knowledge base and workflow automation tools available from the Essentials tier upward
Ticketing system and unlimited task automations on the Plus plan, alongside white-labeling and 100+ integrations
Chat triggers, canned responses/shortcuts, and private internal notes for team collaboration
Native e-commerce integrations for order/customer context inside conversations
Custom email domain and unlimited conversation history retention from the Mini tier up
Enterprise tier with dedicated onboarding, custom SLAs, and team training

faq.question: Is Crisp priced per seat or per workspace?
faq.answer: Per workspace, with a set number of seats bundled into each tier (2 on Free, 4 on Mini, 10 on Essentials, 20+ on Plus) — adding more seats than the bundle typically costs extra rather than being a flat per-user fee.

faq.question: How does Crisp's AI chatbot billing work?
faq.answer: Each paid plan includes a dollar-denominated AI credit pool (e.g. $25 of credits on Essentials, roughly 450 automated conversations) that automated chatbot replies draw down; heavier automation usage requires a higher tier or add-on credits.

faq.question: What channels does Crisp support beyond the website widget?
faq.answer: Crisp connects WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, and email into the same shared inbox alongside the core website chat widget, so agents work every channel from one thread view.

faq.question: Is Crisp a good fit for larger support teams?
faq.answer: It scales up to an Enterprise tier with custom SLAs and dedicated onboarding, but its strongest reputation and pricing sweet spot is small-to-mid-sized teams; larger orgs weighing Zendesk or Intercom should compare ticketing depth and reporting before committing.

faq.question: Why is Crisp's Trustpilot score so much lower than its G2/Capterra scores?
faq.answer: Trustpilot reviews for Crisp skew heavily toward billing and cancellation complaints — customers reporting continued charges after attempting to cancel and friction getting refunds — while G2 and Capterra reviews focus more on day-to-day product usability, where Crisp scores well.

scorecard.note: Widget and shared inbox are quick to stand up; Capterra reviewers repeatedly call the interface intuitive.
One reviewer reported a 40% query reduction from AI handling mundane questions, but the credit-metered automation budget caps how much AI work smaller plans can actually do.
Genuinely unifies web chat, WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, SMS, and email in one inbox — a real strength versus single-channel widgets.
Per-workspace pricing with a generous free tier and mid-tier plans well under Intercom/Zendesk equivalents, though multi-workspace credit structure confuses some buyers.
Praised as responsive in most G2/Capterra reviews, but Trustpilot's 1.9/5 reflects a real subset of billing and cancellation-support complaints worth taking seriously.

pricing.model: Per-workspace tiered SaaS with bundled AI credits

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 2 seats, website widget, shared inbox, mobile apps, contact forms, e-commerce integrations, no AI credits

plans.name: Mini
plans.notes: 4 seats, $5 AI credits (~90 automated conversations), shared email inbox, shortcuts, triggers, private notes, custom email domain

plans.name: Essentials
plans.notes: 10 seats, $25 AI credits (~450 automated conversations), omnichannel inbox, workflow automation, AI chatbot, knowledge base, routing rules

plans.name: Plus
plans.notes: 20+ seats, $75 AI credits (~1,350 automated conversations), unlimited task automations, ticketing, 100+ integrations, white labeling, advanced analytics

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Dedicated onboarding, personalized SLAs, custom features, team training

pricingBreakdown: Crisp prices per workspace, not per seat, which is the detail that makes its numbers look deceptively cheap until you actually count heads: the $45/mo Mini plan bundles 4 seats, which works out to roughly $11/seat if you fill it — versus Intercom's Essential tier at a flat $29/seat/mo no matter your headcount. For a 4-person team, that's Crisp doing an entire inbox, WhatsApp, and social bundle for less than the cost of a single Intercom seat. The catch is the AI credit pool: Mini's $5 of AI credit buys roughly 90 automated conversations a month, which sounds generous until you line it up against Chatbase's Hobby tier ($32/mo for 700 message credits) — Crisp's AI is cheap to add but shallow at the bottom, so if AI automation volume (not seat count) is actually your bottleneck, Essentials ($95/mo, ~450 automated conversations) is the realistic starting point, not Mini. Where Crisp's pricing genuinely earns its 'budget Intercom' reputation is Plus at $295/mo for 20+ seats and unlimited task automations — Intercom doesn't get you anywhere near that headcount without seat pricing multiplying the bill many times over.

capabilities.note: This is Crisp's actual center of gravity — website chat, email, and every connected social/messaging channel land in one thread view, with private internal notes and canned responses for team collaboration. If a unified inbox is the main thing you're shopping for, this is genuinely one of the strongest options at this price point, not a bolted-on afterthought.

The widget and shared inbox stand up fast, and Capterra reviewers repeatedly call the setup intuitive. It's the entry point into everything else Crisp does, and it's the one part of the product that's consistently praised across every review platform, Trustpilot included.

The AI layer trains on your site, files, and Q&A pairs and includes routing rules for escalating to a human when it's out of its depth. One Capterra reviewer specifically credited it with a 40% reduction in incoming queries — a real number worth taking seriously — but remember it's credit-metered per workspace, so heavier automation needs mean upgrading tiers or buying add-on credits, not a flat unlimited allowance.

Available from the Essentials tier ($95/mo) up, paired with workflow automation tools. It's there to feed the AI layer and support agents alike, but it's not the standalone, deeply-featured knowledge base product you'd get from a dedicated helpdesk platform — think of it as functional, not a differentiator.

Native e-commerce integrations surface order and customer context directly inside a conversation, which matters more in practice than a generic CRM field list — an agent can see what someone actually bought without tab-switching. It's solid for support-driven contact context, less built out as a full marketing-CRM replacement.

This is the one area where Crisp is honestly thinner than its reputation elsewhere — chat triggers and canned responses exist, but independent hands-on reviews specifically call out limited marketing functionality on social channels. If proactive campaign broadcasting across channels is a core requirement, look elsewhere first and treat anything here as a bonus, not a reason to buy.

pros: Genuinely unified omnichannel inbox (web, WhatsApp, social, SMS, email) rather than a chat widget with bolt-on channels
Free tier is usable enough that small teams can run real support before ever paying
Self-funded and profitable company history suggests low risk of a sudden pivot or shutdown driven by investor pressure
Strong day-to-day usability scores across major review platforms
cons: Trustpilot rating (1.9/5) reveals a real pattern of billing and cancellation complaints that the higher-profile review sites don't fully surface
AI automation is credit-metered per workspace, so heavier automation needs mean upgrading tiers or buying add-on credits
Message-delivery reliability issues appear in a non-trivial number of independent reviews
Advanced features (ticketing, white-labeling, 100+ integrations) are locked behind the $295/mo Plus tier

sentiment.quote: The tool is awesome, the support team very reactive if you need anything. What more can we ask for?
Crisp often doesn't send our support team's responses to our users, and when we bring this up with them it takes a lot of arguing and persistence to finally fix it.
It's value for money already bringing us a 40% reduction in queries due to their AI handling mundane queries on behalf of our agents.

bestFor: Small-to-mid-sized teams wanting one inbox for web chat, WhatsApp, and social messaging without enterprise pricing
Budget-conscious startups that need a usable free tier before committing to a paid plan
Teams prioritizing omnichannel breadth over deep AI automation sophistication
Companies wary of vendor instability who value a self-funded, profitable operator
verdict: Crisp is the honest budget pick in this category, and the math backs it up, not just the marketing: a genuinely unified inbox across web, WhatsApp, and social for $45-95/mo is a fraction of what Intercom charges per seat, from a company that's stayed self-funded for a decade instead of chasing a Series B that would eventually need to be repaid through your invoice. The catch is the split personality in its own reviews — G2 and Capterra reviewers who actually use it day-to-day rate it highly, while Trustpilot's 1.9/5 is dragged down by a real, specific thread of billing and cancellation complaints that's hard to wave away as noise. My honest read: if you're the kind of team that reads the fine print on auto-renewal and AI-credit consumption before signing, Crisp is a strong pick that punches well above its price. If you tend to sign up and forget to check back in, that Trustpilot score is describing exactly the kind of billing surprise that catches people like that off guard.
